body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}\), characterize the Pareto frontier of universal exact separator schemes for \(\mathfrak S_p\) in the two coordinates consisting of the maximum number of active target blocks and the maximum rational height. In particular, determine for which \(p\) the achieved pair \((2,\lceil\log_2p\rceil)\) can be improved in either coordinate without worsening the other, while every scheme must still separate every pair with unequal static signatures by an observable polynomial certificate.
body.justification: The upper bound is operationally sharp only after the unavoidable support and arithmetic costs of universal separation are understood.
body.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 supplies no witness-complexity notion, while general rational-identifiability arguments do not resolve minimum support or height on this blocked class.
body.consumer: A lower frontier would certify whether any exact equivalence tester can use a smaller numerical alphabet or fewer activated communities than the binary-star library.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact Pareto frontier of the maximum active-block count and maximum rational height for universal separator schemes remains undetermined.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the admissible scheme class, normalization of polynomial certificates, or which numerical objects contribute to height.  Without those choices, rescaling a certificate changes its recorded height and unrestricted non-star source parameters make active-block support incomparable, so a universal lower-bound statement is not well typed.  Even after restricting to unit-noise rational source covariances and the two frozen certificate formats, proving that one active block or a smaller height cannot separate all unequal signatures requires a new crossing-partition lower-bound construction not supplied by the core.
obligation.attempted: I reduced the support lower bound to the empty-graph versus one-edge pair and examined the crossing-partition and unequal-family reversed-edge cases used by the upper router.  They prove necessity of some nonzero activation but do not rule out a different one-block covariance or a lower-height nonbinary choice.
obligation.partial_result: Within the frozen binary-star construction, \(\texttt{thm:bounded-binary-star-separation}\) supplies the upper point \((2,\lceil\log_2p\rceil)\).  For every \(p\ge2\), any source-SEM separator must activate at least one block: no activation with unit innovations returns \(I_p\), which belongs to every state model by setting all structural coefficients to zero, while unequal signatures exist between the empty graph and a one-edge graph.  Hence the first coordinate is at least \(1\), and height is nonnegative.  The frozen core does not decide whether one block can be universal or whether height below \(\lceil\log_2p\rceil\) is possible.
